title: RT-J: Large-Scale Pretraining of Relational Transformers for Context-Efficient Predictions
claim: Training proceeds through a sequence of sampling, retrieval, context-building and prediction stages that turn raw relational databases into model training examples.
layout: 6 numbered panels in 2 rows, snake-like flow, row two reads right-to-left
description: A six-step training recipe laid out as numbered panels in two rows. The top row runs left to right. Panel 1 shows sampling a random database and task (autocomplete or forecast targets) from the Join, with a schema of linked tables (user, txn, item, sales). Panel 2 shows tables connected by foreign-key links, with the target table and target row highlighted and future rows dropped. Panel 3 shows many random walks over the table graph, with visit counts listed beside the candidate target rows. The bottom row runs right to left. Panel 4 shows local BFS trees at 1K, 2K and 4K cell budgets, with the hyperparameters shown as pill selectors. Panel 5 shows the assembled context window with red question-mark mask tokens. Panel 6 shows RT-J predicting the masked cells, drawn as isometric grids with a loss shown on the masked cells. Dark green marks the target and red marks masking and the model. Large numbered circle badges guide the eye through the steps.
caption: RT-J pretraining recipe. (1) We sample a database and prediction task from THE JOIN. The task specifies the target table and the target column. (2) We sample a target row from the target table. Rows after the target row’s timestamp are dropped; kept target-table rows form the candidate in-context examples. (3) From the target row, many parallel random walks rank candidate examples by visit count, on the fly. (4) We process candidate examples in descending visit-count order, using each as the root of a local bounded-width breadth-first-search (BFS) over primary–foreign key links; the context size and BFS hyperparameters are sampled randomly. (5) The collected rows form the context window for the relational transformer (RT), which treats cells as tokens. The target table rows in the context enable in-context learning. The target cell is always masked; non-target cells may be masked optionally. (6) RT-J predicts all masked cells and is trained against their ground-truth values.
abstract: Foundation models for tables and relational databases are increasingly used for predictive tasks across various scientific and industrial domains. However, adapting existing models to unseen datasets requires tens of thousands of examples. Here we introduce RT-J, an 86M-parameter relational foundation model (RFM) that makes accurate predictions even with hundreds of in-context examples or fewer. To achieve this, we first assemble the Join, a large collection of 639 web-crawled databases with 6,023 LLM-generated forecasting tasks. We pretrain with long contexts of up to 8,192 database cells, using in-context examples from a novel lightweight random-walk retriever. Finally, we leverage context tuning and ensembling to scale up test-time compute. On in-context regression tasks from RelBench, RT-J requires 10x fewer examples on average to match strong feature engineering pipelines with LLM-agent or RDBLearn featurizers and TabICLv2 or LightGBM predictors. Overall, our work pushes the frontier for context-efficient predictions on relational data and highlights the importance of real-world semantics, context engineering and large-scale pretraining for RFMs.
